study_identification_part.si_4_title: Cortical thickness deviations as biomarker for subtyping and prognosis in pediatric brainstem tumors

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The study used Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), a Bayesian technique implemented in Python 3.9 and PCNToolkit 0.22, to create region-specific normative models for cortical thickness across 210 distinct cerebral regions. Models were validated through 10-fold cross-validation on the healthy control dataset.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: We used Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), a Bayesian technique implemented in Python 3.9 and PCNToolkit 0.22, to create region-specific models.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Jia2025.pdf.md: Materials and methods / Normative modeling

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: The study modeled cortical thickness (CTh) measured from 3D T1-weighted MRI scans using CAT12 toolbox (version 12.7). The cortex was parcellated into 210 distinct regions using the Human Brainnetome Atlas, and the mean CTh for each region was calculated.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: For each individual, CTh was calculated using the CAT12 toolbox (version 12.7). The procedure involved segmenting MRI data to distinguish gray matter, white matter, and cerebrospinal fluid. Then, the pial surface and gray matter/white matter boundary were reconstructed, and CTh was measured as the distance between the corresponding vertices.
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Jia2025.pdf.md: Materials and methods / MRI acquisition and processing

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: The normative model incorporated age, gender (sex), and total intracranial volume (TIV) as covariates. These same covariates were also used in the ComBat harmonization process to account for inter-scanner variability while preserving biological variability.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: We incorporate age, gender and TIV as covariates.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.location: Jia2025.pdf.md: Materials and methods / Normative modeling
